Alright, let me think through this year's cotton on my 13.1 mu.

I've been growing cotton here for a long time now. My land is all in cotton — no wheat, no maize. That's how it is in our village on this side of Quzhou. The soil is alright, a bit salty in one corner but workable. I know this ground.

**Planting.** I'll plant around April 20th, maybe a couple days either side depending on how the soil warms up. If we get a cold snap I wait — planting into cold ground is asking for poor emergence and I learned that lesson years ago. I use mulch film, everyone does here, it warms the soil and keeps weeds down early.

**Seed.** I buy new seed every year, a hybrid variety. Saving cotton seed doesn't really work — the hybrid vigor is gone by the next generation and yields drop. I usually get whatever my seed dealer recommends that my neighbors have had decent results with. Last year's variety did okay so I might stick with it, maybe around 50 yuan per mu for seed.

**Fertilizer.** This is where I think carefully. Last year I put down a compound fertilizer before planting — about 40 kg per mu of 15-15-15, that gives me roughly 6 kg N, 6 kg P, 6 kg K per mu as the base. Then when the cotton starts flowering in July I topdress urea, about 20 kg per mu, which is another 9 kg N or so. So total N comes to around 15 kg per mu. The extension man has said 18 is better but urea has gotten expensive and I'd rather save a bit of cash than chase the last few kg of yield. Phosphorus and potassium I only put down at base — no topdress for those.

**Irrigation.** I have a tube well. Cotton doesn't need as much water as wheat but it does need water at flowering and boll-setting. Last year was dry so I watered three times. Normally two times is enough — once before flowering in late June or early July, once during boll development in August if it's been dry. Pumping costs money, the electricity adds up, so I don't water if the rain has been good.

**Pesticide.** Cotton needs spraying, there's no way around it. Bollworms, aphids, sometimes spider mites. I'll spray maybe 4-5 times through the season — insecticide mainly, and I put down a herbicide once early after planting for weeds between the mulch strips. I watch my plants, if I don't see pests I don't spray that round. No point wasting money.

**Tillage.** I plow in early April before planting, one deep plow and then a harrow to smooth it. Nothing fancy. I hire a small tractor since I don't own one — costs around 40-50 yuan per mu for the plowing.

**Labor.** My wife and I do most of the work. My older kids help at picking time — that's the big labor crunch, cotton picking takes weeks and we do multiple picks from September into October. Two of my kids work in town but they come back for the big picking days. If we can't keep up I'll hire a few neighbors by the day during peak picking, maybe 100 yuan per person per day. Picking alone probably takes 50-60 person-days across the season on 13 mu.

**Yield.** Last year I got about 260 kg of lint per mu. If the weather cooperates and the pests aren't bad I'm hoping for 280 this year, but I don't count on it. Cotton is fussy — one bad hailstorm in August and you lose a lot.

**Budget thinking.** Seed, fertilizer, pesticide, irrigation, plowing, maybe some hired labor at picking — I'm spending something like 1,000-1,200 yuan per mu in inputs before my own labor. With 13.1 mu that's around 14-15 thousand yuan going in. Cotton price this year will decide whether it's worth it. I don't have another crop to fall back on so I pay attention to the market.
